description: Compile-time arity checking for JACL (M7). Catch wrong-argument-count errors at compile time for statically resolvable proc calls and builtins. Track arity through variable assignments. Extend JaclClosure with arity metadata.

userStories.title: Extend JaclClosure with arity metadata
userStories.description: As a developer of the JACL runtime, I want JaclClosure to carry arity metadata so it is available for compile-time checking and future variadic support.
acceptanceCriteria: JaclClosure struct in bytecode.c gains a 'variadic' bool field (set to false for now) and a 'min_args' uint8_t field (equal to param_count for fixed-arity procs)
Compiler populates variadic and min_args when creating closures in compiler.c
Existing runtime arity check in OP_CALL (vm.c) continues to function using param_count
No change to the JaclVal 64-bit tagged-value encoding — metadata lives on the heap JaclClosure struct
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
All existing tests pass (build.sh)

userStories.title: Compiler local table arity tracking
userStories.description: As a developer of the JACL compiler, I need the Local struct to optionally carry arity information so the compiler can check calls through variables.
acceptanceCriteria: Local struct in compiler.c gains an arity tracking field (e.g., int16_t known_arity where -1 means unknown)
When a local is initialized from a proc definition, known_arity is set to that proc's param_count
When a local is initialized from another local with known arity (e.g., def g f where f has known arity), known_arity propagates
When a local's source arity is unknown (runtime expression, non-proc value), known_arity is -1
Arity information is scoped correctly — does not leak across scope boundaries
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
All existing tests pass (build.sh)

userStories.title: Compile-time arity error for direct proc calls
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the compiler to reject [foo 1 2 3] when foo is defined as [proc foo [a b] { ... }] so that I catch mistakes before running my program.
acceptanceCriteria: Compiler emits an error when a command head resolves to a known proc and the argument count does not match param_count
Error message includes line, column, proc name, expected count, and actual count (e.g., 'line 5, col 1: proc 'foo' expects 2 arguments but got 3')
Compilation fails (non-zero error_count) and no bytecode is executed
Existing valid programs continue to compile and run unchanged
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
All existing tests pass (build.sh)

userStories.title: Arity checking through variable assignments
userStories.description: As a developer, I want arity checking to work when I bind a proc to a variable, so that [def f add3] [f 1 2] is caught at compile time.
acceptanceCriteria: When def binds a local to a value whose arity is known (a proc literal or another local with known arity), calls through that local are checked
Calls through a local with known arity produce compile-time errors on mismatch
When the bound value's arity is unknown, no compile-time check occurs and the call compiles normally
Arity info propagates through simple alias chains: [def g f] inherits f's arity when f is known
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
All existing tests pass (build.sh)

userStories.title: Builtin arity enforcement audit
userStories.description: As a developer, I want consistent arity errors for all builtins so that typos and missing arguments are caught early.
acceptanceCriteria: All existing builtins have arity constraints enforced in the compiler
Fixed-arity builtins (def: 2, proc: 3, print: 1, +: 2, -: 2, *: 2, /: 2, =: 2, <: 2, >: 2) produce compile-time errors on mismatch
Flexible-arity builtins (if: 2-3, slice: 2-3, concat: 2+) produce errors when outside their valid range
Error messages follow the same format as user proc arity errors (line, col, name, expected, got)
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
All existing tests pass (build.sh)

userStories.title: Arity checking test suite
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a comprehensive test suite that validates arity checking behavior so that regressions are caught.
acceptanceCriteria: test/jacl/arity_direct.jacl — direct call with too few args produces compile error (# expect-error:)
test/jacl/arity_direct_many.jacl — direct call with too many args produces compile error
test/jacl/arity_correct.jacl — direct calls with correct arg counts compile and run
test/jacl/arity_alias.jacl — call through variable alias with wrong arity produces compile error
test/jacl/arity_alias_correct.jacl — call through alias with correct arity compiles and runs
test/jacl/arity_unknown.jacl — call through unknown-arity variable compiles without error
test/jacl/arity_builtins.jacl — builtin with wrong arity produces compile error (at least if, def, +)
test/jacl/arity_nested.jacl — nested proc definitions with separate arities checked independently
All new tests pass; entire existing test suite remains green
All tests pass as part of build.sh
